references.text: Rachel gives her maidservant Bilhah to Jacob so that she may bear children on Rachel's behalf – the immediate context of this verse.
Jacob names his son Dan, and Bilhah later bears another son, Naphtali – a direct follow-up to Bilhah's childbirth.
A parallel situation where Sarai gives her maidservant Hagar to Abram to bear children, a similar surrogacy motif.
Describes the birth of Jacob's first four sons with Leah, which forms the background for the rivalry that leads to Bilhah's role.
Summarizes Bilhah's sons Dan and Naphtali as part of the list of Jacob's twelve sons.
The specific birth of Dan highlights the fulfillment of the genealogy and God's faithfulness to the promise of fruitfulness.
Bilhah appears as an instrument of God's promise in one verse, while her role becomes the source of family division and loss of privilege in the other.
